name: Carnivore diet breath
lead: Carnivore diet breath refers to the bad breath or unusual breath odour that some people report when eating only animal products, a pattern commonly called the carnivore or zero-carb diet.[1] Within appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a social and grooming concern, alongside other low-carbohydrate or ketogenic eating patterns.

The carnivore diet is a high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet that excludes plant foods.[1] Reference works on bad breath mention acetone, produced in ketosis and uncontrolled diabetes, as a source of a fruity breath odour, and list fasting among less common causes.[2] Published clinical studies specific to breath on a carnivore diet were not found.
infobox: None found specific to carnivore diets

paras: The carnivore diet permits only animal products such as meat, dairy and eggs, and excludes plant foods; stricter versions allow only beef, salt and water.[1] Encyclopedic summaries of the diet list reported adverse effects including low fibre intake, possible vitamin deficiencies and raised LDL cholesterol, and do not discuss breath.[1]

Halitosis is most often attributed to oral causes such as tongue coating, gum disease and tooth decay.[2] Acetone, a ketone body, is linked to a fruity breath smell, and ketoacidosis and fasting are listed among less common causes.[2] Some people who eat very low-carbohydrate diets attribute breath changes to ketosis; whether this applies to carnivore eating specifically has not been established in published studies.

General guidance for halitosis includes cleaning the tongue, brushing, flossing, antimicrobial mouthwash and treating underlying gum or dental disease.[2] The same article states that evidence does not support dietary changes as a treatment for bad breath.[2]

card.summary: Reports of bad breath on an all-meat diet; the idea is discussed, but no studies on carnivore breath specifically exist.
card.note: Persistent bad breath can have dental or medical causes.

quick.overview:
Carnivore diet breath is the bad breath some people report when eating only animal products. It is mentioned in discussions of the diet and of keto-style eating.

No clinical studies were found that measure breath on a carnivore diet.
quick.mechanism: Reference sources link acetone from ketosis to a fruity breath odour, but oral causes such as tongue coating and gum disease are the most common cause of halitosis in general.
quick.risks: The odour itself is not described as harmful. Dentists and physicians advise evaluation when bad breath persists, since gum disease, decay or conditions such as diabetes can be causes.
